translator: Claude (AI), draft, not reviewed by a Hittitologist
intro: A late New Script anthology tablet with two augurs' rituals against dying in the army camp. The first is by Maddunani (also read Madduwani), augur of Arzawa (§0–4), and is largely broken. The second is the four-day ritual of the augur Dandanku (§5–19): fodder and coloured wool go to the horses and servants of the god Iyarri, animals are cut apart for the Sebettu, and a donkey (a clay one for a poor man) carries the evil into the enemy land. The colophon calls this the first tablet (§20).

sections.title: Ritual of Maddunani, augur of Arzawa

paras.en: Thus (says) Maddunani, the augur, man of Arzawa: If a plague breaks out in the army camps, and people, horses and cattle are dying heavily, then they perform a mūranza-ritual (meaning unclear).

They perform it as follows: two puppies, one piglet, twelve thick loaves of a tarna-measure, among them one ḫulliti- (meaning unclear), fourteen purpura-(balls) of bread, two handfuls of unhusked(?) kant-grain, six cups, one set of GÌR.GÁN-vessels, one ḫabḫab-jug of wine. I take all this.
Then at night I prepare (it). But when it grows light, the augur and the old man […] away through the midst of the army camps […], and meanwhile they speak as follows:

'[…] in an evil way, somewhere […] […] they …ed. If some evil (person) […] has done something to him […] some [evi]l bird […] … all […]' […] the limb(?) […] […] […] away(?) […] [— break at the end of column I —] Then, when they perform (the ritual), they take (as an omen) a bird coming up from behind(?); and when they complete the ritual, they take (as an omen) a bird coming after it(?).
This ritual the old man and the augur set about performing.
Thus (says) Dandanku, the augur: If there is continual dying in the army camps, they perform this ritual:

They take a fodder mixture mixed together, grain and straw, and red wool, blue wool, black wool and white wool. They mix the grain and straw together and scatter it across the ḫaddari- of the road (crossroads?), and he speaks as follows:

'The grooms who are yours, (those) of the god Iyarri: let them give this fodder mixture to the horses! And let the maidservants of the god take the red wool, blue wool, black wool, green wool and white wool!'

Afterwards he takes one kid, one piglet and one puppy, and they cut them apart for the Sebettu (the 'Seven') in an untouched place, across (the way). Afterwards he libates [beer and wine(?)] to [the Sebettu], each three times.
[…] they come [aw]ay. […] is finished.
[…] exactly the same. […]

[…] they perform, and they take these (things): […] emmer, one cheese, one sour (loaf), […] one jug of beer, one bowl of wine, […] two billy goats [— break —] […] they […]. [Then] the ritual patron [… to] dr[ink …] […] [he drinks (to) Iy]arri three [times] […] […]
[…] Iyarri (and) the Sebettu […] […]
[…] he drinks.
[… the maid]servants, the staff-bearers, the c[ooks …] […] he drinks three times.

[When] they have provided […] to eat and to drink, [then] the ritual [patron] steps up, and they drive up a donkey. But if (he is) a poor man, they make a donkey of clay. Then they turn it with its eyes towards the enemy land and speak as follows: 'You, Iyarri, have done evil to this land and to the army camps. Now let this donkey lift it up and carry it into the enemy land!'
Afterwards they draw a bow and set an arrow (to it); but the arrows he scatters down in front, and he speaks: 'O god, keep shooting at the enemy land from here with the arrow!
But when you come into the land of Ḫatti, let your quiver be closed, and let your bow be unstrung!' And they come away.

On the fourth day, when it grows light: three billy goats, twenty-six thick loaves of a tarna-measure, three warm loaves, three GÚG-breads, three sweet breads, three jugs of beer, ten cups, […] GÌR.GÁN-vessel(s) […]
[…] … […] […] and for each god […] he places, and they eat. And they drink (to) Iyarri again and again, [and t]o Iyarri (and) the Sebettu(?).
[Colophon:] First tablet, complete. 'If in the army camp there is heavy dying.'
